defects.title: Anonymous POST /api/v1/agencies/seed-defaults writes to the database
defects.desc: The endpoint was marked [AllowAnonymous]. Any unauthenticated caller could insert demo carrier agencies into a production database, polluting the agency list the AI matching pipeline chooses from.
defects.steps: 1. Start the API. 2. `curl -X POST http://localhost:5159/api/v1/agencies/seed-defaults` with no Authorization header. 3. Observe HTTP 200 and seeded agencies.
defects.fix: AgenciesController.SeedDefaultAgencies now `[Authorize(Roles = Admin)]`. Commit message references DEF-001 (`git log --grep=DEF-001`).
defects.retest: SeedEndpoints_Return401_ForAnonymousCaller, SeedEndpoints_Return403_ForShipper and SeedDefaultAgencies_Succeeds_ForAdmin all pass (before: 8 of 47 SecurityTests failed, after: 0 of 47).

defects.title: Anonymous POST /api/v1/trips/seed-example writes a full trip hierarchy
defects.desc: Same class of flaw as DEF-001 on the Trips controller: [AllowAnonymous] 'for convenient local dev use' creates users, loads, assignments and trips on whatever database the API points at.
defects.steps: 1. `curl -X POST http://localhost:5159/api/v1/trips/seed-example` with no token. 2. Observe HTTP 200 and the seeded trips in the body.
defects.fix: TripsController.SeedExample now `[Authorize(Roles = Admin)]`. Commit message references DEF-002.
defects.retest: Same SeedEndpoints_* tests, parameterised over both URLs, pass.

defects.title: Internal API key is checked after model validation
defects.desc: InternalApiKeyAuthFilter was an action filter, so a caller with no or a wrong X-Internal-Api-Key and an invalid body received HTTP 400 with validation details instead of 401. Unauthenticated callers could probe the request schema.
defects.steps: 1. POST `{}` to /internal/agent-workflow-runs with no X-Internal-Api-Key. 2. Observe 400 (expected 401).
defects.fix: Filter now implements IAsyncAuthorizationFilter, which runs before model binding. Commit message references DEF-003.
defects.retest: InternalEndpoints_RejectMissingOrWrongServiceKey (3 cases) and InternalEndpoints_RejectUserJwt_InPlaceOfServiceKey pass; the existing InternalPricing/AgentWorkflowRuns controller tests still pass.

defects.title: API crashes on startup against real PostgreSQL when no Admin exists
defects.desc: SeedDefaultPricingConfigIfNotExistsAsync used a random Guid as SetByUserId when no Admin user existed. EF Core's InMemory provider ignores foreign keys, so the 560+ existing tests never noticed; on PostgreSQL the insert violates FK_FuelPriceRates_Users_SetByUserId (23503) and the host fails to start.
defects.found_by: New Postgres end-to-end workflow test (area E) on Testcontainers PostgreSQL
defects.steps: 1. Start the API (Development) against an empty PostgreSQL with ADMIN_USER_EMAIL / ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD unset. 2. Startup throws DbUpdateException 23503.
defects.fix: Seed is skipped (with a warning) when no Admin exists; the next start after an Admin exists seeds the defaults. Commit message references DEF-004.
defects.retest: Before: 5 of 7 targeted tests failed. After: 7 of 7 pass, including 3 new unit tests (no-admin, with-admin, idempotent) and the 4 Postgres E2E tests.

defects.title: File endpoints return HTTP 500 when Cloudinary is not configured
defects.desc: OWASP ZAP reported 10 HTTP 500 responses (and 'Application Error Disclosure') on /api/v1/files/*. With no Cloudinary credentials the singleton Cloudinary client fails to build and every call becomes a generic 500. The response body is the standard error envelope (no stack trace), and .env.example already documents that uploads require Cloudinary, so this is a configuration-dependent robustness issue rather than a data exposure.
defects.steps: 1. Run the API without CLOUDINARY_* settings. 2. GET /api/v1/files/content/x or POST /api/v1/files/single with a valid token. 3. Observe HTTP 500.
defects.fix: Recommended: validate Cloudinary options at startup or return 503 from CloudinaryFileStorageService when unconfigured. Not changed: out of scope for the testing work and needs a team decision on fail-fast vs. 503.
defects.retest: Retest scan still reports the 10 x 500 alert (expected for an open defect). Production deployments set the Cloudinary variables.

defects.title: Responses lack X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
defects.desc: OWASP ZAP rule 10021: API, error and Swagger responses were served without X-Content-Type-Options, allowing MIME sniffing.
defects.fix: Small middleware in Program.cs adds the header to every response, including errors. Commit message references DEF-006.
defects.retest: Responses_CarryNosniffHeader_IncludingErrors (4 cases) pass: before 4 of 52 SecurityTests failed, after 0. ZAP retest: the X-Content-Type-Options alert is gone (WARN 6 -> 5, PASS 114 -> 115).

observations.text: Marketplace accept bypasses the AI/Shipper approval step. AssignmentService.ApproveAsync lets any Agency Staff accept a Posted load directly (creating a stub 'Completed' workflow run). This looks deliberate (marketplace feature) so it is not logged as a defect, but the team should confirm it is intended, because it means an agency can take a load the Shipper never approved.
Model-binding errors expose a framework type name, e.g. 'could not be converted to System.Decimal'. Low-impact information disclosure; fix by customising the model-state error messages.
ZAP 'Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy missing' (Low) is intentionally not changed: the API is consumed cross-origin by the React and Flutter clients, so a restrictive CORP value could break them.
ZAP 'Timestamp Disclosure - Unix' on /auth/me is a false positive (an id/creation value that merely looks like an epoch).
Backend branch coverage is about 52% against about 92% line coverage; most remaining gaps are error branches in services.
